title: Rewarding Noise: Incentives in Decentralized A/B Testing
abstract: arXiv:2610.19512v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many firms that run A/B tests struggle with low statistical power, increasing the risk that launch decisions are driven by noise rather than true impact. We argue that in decentralized organizations, low power can reflect misaligned incentives: product teams choose what and how to test on a customer-facing experience to maximize their private reward, while the experience owner sets evaluation rules and launch criteria to optimize the experience. We formalize this interaction via a principal-agent model and show that evaluating tests using raw impact estimates creates a reward to sampling noise. Correctly calibrated posterior-mean evaluation removes this reward and creates a local incentive to reallocate toward fewer, more precise tests of more ambitious ideas. Using data on A/B tests run at Amazon, we document patterns consistent with these model predictions. After an Amazon experience shifted to posterior-mean-based evaluation in 2024,

translated_title: 奖励噪声：去中心化A/B测试中的激励机制
translated_abstract: 许多运行A/B测试的公司都面临统计功效低下的问题，这增加了发布决策由噪声而非真实影响驱动的风险。我们认为，在去中心化的组织中，低统计功效可能反映了激励机制的错位：产品团队为了最大化自身回报而选择在面向客户的体验上测试什么以及如何测试，而体验所有者则制定评估规则和发布标准以优化体验。我们通过委托-代理模型将这种互动形式化，并证明使用原始影响估计来评估测试会产生对抽样噪声的奖励。正确校准的后验均值评估消除了这种奖励，并产生了将资源重新分配到更少、更精确地测试更具雄心的想法的局部激励。利用亚马逊运行的A/B测试数据，我们记录了与这些模型预测一致的模式。在2024年亚马逊某项体验转向基于后验均值的评估之后，
tldr: 该论文通过委托-代理模型揭示，去中心化组织中A/B测试统计功效低下源于激励错位——基于原始影响估计的评估会奖励抽样噪声，而正确校准的后验均值评估可消除这种激励，促使团队转向更少但更精确、更具雄心的测试，并利用亚马逊的实际数据验证了这些预测。
en_tdlr: This paper uses a principal-agent model to show that low statistical power in decentralized A/B testing stems from misaligned incentives—evaluating tests with raw impact estimates rewards sampling noise, while correctly calibrated posterior-mean evaluation eliminates this reward and incentivizes fewer, more precise tests of more ambitious ideas, with predictions validated using Amazon A/B testing data.
